title: Prove the star-pattern floor n+1 on the wheel W4 and K33 at minimum degree 3 (no κ)
body:
## Result

No κ claim, no word and no supplier change.

For a simple graph Γ on `n` points, `G_Γ` is the star-configuration graph of #7114: points and edges of Γ as vertices, a point adjacent to the pairs containing it, two pairs adjacent iff disjoint. A k-block pattern has invertible diagonal blocks and zero blocks on non-adjacent pairs; `H_f(G;F)` is the infimum of rank/k.

**Theorem 1.** For Γ the wheel `W_4` (`n = 5`) and Γ = `K_{3,3}` (`n = 6`), every k-block pattern on `G_Γ` has rank at least `(n+1)k`, for every `k` and every field. With the Gram upper bound of #7114, `H_f(G_{W_4};F) = 6` and `H_f(G_{K_{3,3}};F) = 7` over every field. Both graphs have minimum degree 3 and contain no `K_4`.

**Corollary 2.** In a star configuration `(K, Γ, (T_e))` with `|K| = m`, if Γ has a subgraph isomorphic to `W_4` or `K_{3,3}`, every k-block pattern has rank at least `(m+1)k`; in the notation of #7114 Theorem 3', `j >= k`. #7114 proves this when every non-isolated vertex of Γ has degree at least 4.

**Corollary 3.** All 26 labelled graphs on five points with minimum degree at least 3 contain `W_4`, so Corollary 2 covers each of them.

**Remark 4.** `H_f(G_{C_n};F) = n` for every cycle, so the floor `n+1` can fail at minimum degree 2.

Claim types: Theorem 1 is a finite certificate (two exact rational duals) combined with a scoped written proof that such a dual bounds every block pattern. Corollary 2 and Remark 4 are scoped written proofs. Corollary 3 is an exhaustive count. No statement is made for all graphs of minimum degree 3.

## Evidence

- `certificates.json`: 86 dual entries for `W_4` and 197 for `K_{3,3}`. Each entry is one instance of "a vertex adds at most one" or of elementary submodularity, with a positive rational multiplier.
- `verify.py` (standard library, exact `Fraction` arithmetic) averages every entry over the automorphisms of Γ (8 and 72), applies the decoding closure, and checks that the combination is exactly `f(empty) >= n+1`. It rebuilds the Gram labels as an integer matrix and checks unit diagonal and zeros on non-adjacent pairs. It enumerates the 27 labelled graphs of minimum degree at least 3 on four and five points, builds rank-`n` patterns for cycles of length 3 to 6, and runs 14 rejecting controls (damaged certificates, a deleted edge, a moved edge, a removed adjacency).
- README section 2 gives the rank argument: for a k-block pattern with row space `W`, `f(S) = dim(W + E_S)/k` satisfies normalization, slope, submodularity and decoding. This is the argument of Tuafo's #1744, restated for a general graph.

## Reproduce

From the repository root:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/star-pattern-degree-three-floor
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/star-pattern-degree-three-floor --check-source-history
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B -W error -X dev research/star-pattern-degree-three-floor/verify.py
```

Any CPython 3.12 works in place of that interpreter path. The verifier ends with

```text
PASS_STAR_PATTERN_DEGREE_THREE_FLOOR graphs=2 controls=14 cycles=4 census=27 no_new_kappa
```

Local results on commit `a8ae38561deb40edbd41b9f8790fab6ac949c0a3`: both registered commands pass (normal and `-O`), about 0.4 s each; `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`; `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with 8 files.

`derive_certificates.py` shows how the duals were found. It needs numpy and scipy, is not registered, and the verifier never imports it.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Two graphs only. The general degree-3 statement is not proved.
- The prism is not certified: the floating-point optimum of its program is 7.0, but the rounded dual was rejected by the exact check. No bound is claimed for it.
- The linear program gives lower bounds only; it meets the Gram upper bound on these two graphs.
- The model is the whole-block mask of #6933 and #7114. Sub-block masks and port-dependent block sizes are not covered.
- The orthogonal 8-sets of P104, P112 and P120 have minimum degree 5, 6 and 7, so their floor 9 does not need this result.
- #7114 is open and unreviewed. Only its definitions and Gram labels are used, and the labels are re-checked here.
- The Petersen case (Γ = `K_4`) is not re-proved; its value 5 is cited from Blasiak, Kleinberg and Lubetzky and from #1744.
- No human or proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Is `j >= k` forced for every star configuration whose Γ has minimum degree at least 3? First test: the cube `Q_3`, which contains none of `K_4`, `W_4`, `K_{3,3}` (20 vertices in `G_Γ`).
2. Does the prism have value 7? It needs an exact dual; the float support has 2,133 orbit variables.
3. What are the values at minimum degree 2 beyond cycles? A local, unshipped run of the same exact pipeline gave lower bounds 9/2 for `K_4` minus an edge and 11/2 for `K_{2,3}`; no upper bound below `n+1` was sought.

## Related open work

- #7127: the same port family (P120 and P104) but a different quantity, the number of ports in a subspace of each dimension. No number is shared with this PR.
- #7114 (DreamingOfClouds): source of the question. It proves `j >= k` at minimum degree 4 and `H_f(Petersen;F) >= 9/2`, and lists the Petersen value as open. This PR computes neither number. The Petersen value 5 is already on main through #1744 and the cited literature.

## Credit

DreamingOfClouds (#6933, #7114): block patterns, star configurations, `G_Γ`, Theorem 3', the Gram upper bound and the open question. Tuafo (#1744): the all-field rank argument and the exact Petersen dual. Blasiak, Kleinberg and Lubetzky: the linear program. Bukh and Cox: `H_f`. The two certificates, the corollaries, the cycle remark and the verifier were produced by Nick Petalas.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At head `a8ae38561deb40edbd41b9f8790fab6ac949c0a3`, [run 42908142215](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42908142215) (job 130151433953) failed in `plan`, and `replay` was skipped because `plan` failed. The evidence for this PR is therefore the local runs listed under Reproduce.

Cause, read from the job log: the "Onboarding helper tests" step ran 760 tests (24 skipped) and exactly one failed,

```text
FAIL: test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record (test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record)
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found in '# CI verification\n\n## Current selected-family replay: #6030 ...
```

On main at `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, `certificates/selected-result.json` has `"reproduce": "make frontier7000-verify"`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still opens with "Current selected-family replay: #6030". The test compares those two files, and this PR changes neither; it adds only `research/star-pattern-degree-three-floor/`.

I checked the failed logs of six other runs from today. Each shows the same single failing test, 760 tests run and 24 skipped: 42905094314 and 42903313790 (other contributors' branches), and 42905202459, 42905330981, 42905806694, 42906716667 (#7125, #7126, #7127, #7128).

No fix, retrigger or re-run was made from this PR.
